source.publication: 2025 Individual Income Tax Booklet (Form ND-1 instructions and tables)
source.section: PDF p.14 Line 6 - Net long-term capital gain exclusion; PDF p.15 Worksheet lines 1-8; Form ND-1 line 6; Form ND-1 lines 1b, 4b, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 25; booklet PDF p.4 (starting point is federal taxable income), PDF p.13 Line 1b, PDF p.16 Line 20, PDF p.29 Tax Rate Schedules, PDF pp.22-28 Tax Table

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 100,000.00 + short-term gain 5,000.00 + long-term gain 20,000.00 = 125,000.00. Federal taxable income = 125,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 109,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form ND-1 line 1b federal taxable income 109,250.00; lines 2-3 additions 0.00, line 4a 0.00; line 4b = 109,250.00. Subtractions: line 6 net long-term capital gain exclusion, 40% x 20,000.00 = 8,000.00. Line 17 total subtractions = 8,000.00. Line 18 North Dakota taxable income = 109,250.00 - 8,000.00 = 101,250.00. Line 19 = 101,250.00. Line 20 tax: 1.95% x (101,250.00 - 48,475.00) = 1.95% x 52,775.00 = 1,029.1125, to the cent 1,029.11; taxable income is 100,000 or more, so the form itself uses the schedule (PDF p.29). Lines 21-23 credits: line 22 marriage penalty credit: not a joint return, so none. Expected credits 0.00. Line 25 net tax = 1,029.11. Worksheet: line 1 Schedule D line 15 20,000.00; line 2 Schedule D line 16 25,000.00; line 3 the smaller, 20,000.00; line 8 = 40% x 20,000.00 = 8,000.00. The short-term gain gets no exclusion.
accepted_approximations: The long-term gain exclusion is applied to long-term gains; the worksheet uses the smaller of net long-term gain and overall net gain, so a net short-term loss reduces it.
